A virtual office is permissive for administrative and correspondence purposes, but for a contract manufacturing entity under ISIC 2610 (PCBA assembly), the tax authorities and registry require actual operational premises, local staff, and equipment to demonstrate commercial substance. A pure virtual mailbox without physical production capacity is inadmissible for Spanish corporate registration and will be challenged under transfer pricing and general anti-abuse rules.

Governing statute

Formation / constitutional filings

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 36 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Standard S.L. share capital must be at least EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and fully paid-in before recording. Cash contributions must be evidenced by a bank deposit certificate; no statutory escrow account is required for monetary contributions. A company may alternatively be formed under the 'formación sucesiva' regime with lower capital, subject to specific profit-distribution restrictions, until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached.

Funding & unlock path: Fire-safety certificate issued by a competent technician and accepted by the municipal fire inspection; structural load inspection certificate prepared by an architect or engineer; electrical installation compliance declaration under the Reglamento Electrotécnico de Baja Tensión; workplace risk-prevention audit under Ley 31/1995; and a municipal compatibility certificate confirming the industrial use is lawful at the chosen address.

Paid-in capital rule: Standard S.L. share capital must be at least EUR 3,000 fully subscribed and fully paid-in before recording. Cash contributions must be evidenced by a bank deposit certificate; no statutory escrow account is required for monetary contributions. A company may alternatively be formed under the 'formación sucesiva' regime with lower capital, subject to specific profit-distribution restrictions, until the EUR 3,000 threshold is reached.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
RESOLVED: The incorporators approve the public deed of incorporation and the articles of association. The share capital is fully subscribed and paid-in in cash by the founding members. The registered office is fixed at Calle Ejemplo 10, 28013 Madrid, Spain. The following officers are appointed: [Full Name], sole administrator (Administrador Único); [Full Name], alternate administrator; and [Full Name], secretary. All appointees accept. The sole administrator is authorized to file the provisional CIF application, execute the mercantile registration, open bank accounts, hire staff, engage external advisors, obtain industrial and environmental permits, and take any ancillary action required to commence the PCBA contract manufacturing activity. This resolution is effective immediately and may be implemented by the administrator without further shareholder consent.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

E-government filing portal

Foreign or non-resident entities obtain NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by registering with AEAT using Form 036/037. Spanish tax representative (gestor) mandatory for non-residents; process completes in 30-60 days with digital certificate issuance.

Spanish tax representative (gestor) mandatory for non-residents; process completes in 30-60 days with digital certificate issuance.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain operates under full capital and current account convertibility as a member of the EU and the euro area. No exchange control permits are required for ordinary trade settlement, profit repatriation, or capital transactions. Profit remittance is unrestricted for an SL once statutory annual accounts are approved, the legal reserve requirement is met, and any applicable Spanish withholding tax on dividends is satisfied; treaty relief may reduce the rate for non-resident shareholders. Settlement in EUR of cross-border flows is entirely free of exchange controls, subject only to statistical declarations and AML/KYC information obligations.

Export proceeds surrender rules

There are no statutory surrender requirements, mandatory conversion ratios, or time limits for export proceeds in Spain under the euro-area framework. A resident exporter may retain receipts in EUR or foreign currency and convert them at freely negotiated market rates. Exports and collections above the statistical threshold must be reported to Banco de España for balance-of-payments statistical purposes, typically through the entity's bank using the applicable declaration form.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting under the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Bank of Spain Law 13/1994, together with the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business (Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa) for foreign investment and exchange-related statistical filings.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium viability. EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) holding a passport under the EEA framework can open euro accounts for a Spanish SL without a branch. These entities are well-suited for collections, supplier payouts, and multi-currency settlement. However, they are not credit institutions and cannot provide trade finance, LC confirmations, or committed FX hedging. Some EMIs impose heightened scrutiny on non-EEA beneficial owners and may restrict wires to Latin American, East Asian, or offshore jurisdictions; a banking-grade correspondent arrangement is advisable for large trade flows.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

High-value electronics procurement to China/Hong Kong linked to PCBA component sourcing

Root cause: High-value electronics procurement to China/Hong Kong linked to PCBA component sourcing

Defense evidence: Signed procurement contracts, supplier certificates of origin, detailed commercial invoices with kilowatt-characterised goods descriptions, HS codes matching the PCB/PCBA scope (8517, 8536, 8542, 9030), packing lists, CMR/airway bills or bills of lading, and downloaded ERP transactions showing physical goods movement from supplier to bonded warehouse or final delivery.
Unusually rapid build-up of account turnover relative to stated equity and bank reference size

Root cause: Unusually rapid build-up of account turnover relative to stated equity and bank reference size

Defense evidence: Audited annual financial statements of the Spanish SL, shareholder structure memorandum with CV and passport details, board-approved business plan and cash-flow forecast for the PCBA contract manufacturing pipeline, existing purchase orders and master supply agreements, and tax/IVA returns evidence consistent with the turnover.
Cross-border dividend or intra-group loan repayment to a non-resident shareholder in a preferential tax treaty jurisdiction

Root cause: Cross-border dividend or intra-group loan repayment to a non-resident shareholder in a preferential tax treaty jurisdiction

Defense evidence: Clear ownership chain with notarised articles of incorporation and tax residence certificates, group transfer pricing documentation aligning with OECD guidelines, signed shareholder loan agreements with arm's-length interest rates, proof of Spanish corporate tax payment and reduced withholding tax treaty application (Form 210 or per treaty), and financial statements showing distributable reserves and legal reserve balance.
Transactions with politically exposed persons (PEPs) or entities incorporated in high-risk third countries (e.g., certain Latin American, Asian, or offshore zones)

Root cause: Transactions with politically exposed persons (PEPs) or entities incorporated in high-risk third countries (e.g., certain Latin American, Asian, or offshore zones)

Defense evidence: Full beneficial ownership register disclosure under Royal Decree 571/2023, independent sanction screening results, certified copies of corporate incorporation documents with apostille, public transparency screening evidence, and a legally binding customer attestation of commercial purpose and non-sanction-linked activity.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

For non-resident shareholder equity or shareholder loan contributions, the compliant route is a SWIFT MT103 wire to the SL's euro account in Spain using the beneficiary IBAN and BIC codes. The sender's bank must provide the exact purpose code, usually a capital transaction / direct investment code such as 'GD' or the OECD/EU standard Balance of Payments purpose code for equity acquisitions, accompanied by a clear payment narrative referencing the company's CIF and the investment intent. Within one month of capital injection, the SL must file a foreign investment declaration with the Trade Registry (Registro Mercantil) and the Ministry of Economy under Spanish foreign investment regulations; when the investment exceeds the statutory threshold, a prior screen may be required. For any loan disbursement, execute and keep the signed financing agreement, identify the ECB/EURIBOR benchmark or fixed rate, and report the loan in the Bank of Spain's balance-of-payments statistics through the banking platform.Outbound settlement for the PCBA contract manufacturing activity uses the standard Euro and international corridors. For direct payments to suppliers or subcontractors, SWIFT MT103 messages carry the payment, with beneficiary bank's BIC and IBAN; for correspondent-bank-cleared currencies, MT202 is appended as the cover payment. For supply-chain purchases from non-EU parties, irrevocable documentary letters of credit are issued subject to ICC UCP600, typically payable at sight via an advising bank; for Eurozone suppliers, SEPA Credit Transfers or SEPA Instant are used for smaller operational disbursements, while SWIFT remains the rail for non-EEA and exotic currency payments. Every disbursement must be matched with the underlying order, invoice, and customs/border documentation for AML and tax compliance. Trade finance products such as open-account with buyer credit, back-to-back LCs, and invoice financing can be layered for the contract manufacturing cycle.Spot EUR/USD, EUR/CNH, EUR/LatAm currency outrights for immediate settlementOutright FX forwards (FXA) with tenors matched to known trade settlement datesNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted currencies, primarily when the counterparty rupee, Argentine peso, or certain Latin American currencies may be required and the counterparty bank supports NDF as a hedgeCross-currency swaps for long-term financing of the Spanish SL's euro-denominated working capital or for swapping shareholder loan currency exposureFX options (European-style) for protecting margins on large PCBA tender bidsCurrency swaps structured under master agreement terms and subject to MiFID/ESMA derivatives regulations for non-ultimate-consumers

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium viability. EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) holding a passport under the EEA framework can open euro accounts for a Spanish SL without a branch. These entities are well-suited for collections, supplier payouts, and multi-currency settlement. However, they are not credit institutions and cannot provide trade finance, LC confirmations, or committed FX hedging. Some EMIs impose heightened scrutiny on non-EEA beneficial owners and may restrict wires to Latin American, East Asian, or offshore jurisdictions; a banking-grade correspondent arrangement is advisable for large trade flows.

Statutory Filing Calendar

Statutory deliverableDeadline window Government feeDelinquency sanctions
Annual Accounts and General Meeting approvals (Cuentas Anuales, Junta General, Deposito de Cuentas) Approval by shareholders' meeting within first 6 months after fiscal year-end; deposit with the Commercial Registry within 1 month after approval; for 31 December year-end, latest deposit is approximately 30 July. $0 USD Late deposit triggers 'cierre registral' (registry closure), preventing registration of any subsequent corporate or share transfers; administrative fines up to EUR 300 and possible loss of good standing; persistent non-compliance may lead to judicial dissolution and final deregistration.
Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200) Between the 1st and 25th day of the month following the 6-month period after the fiscal year-end; for 31 December year-end, filing window is 1-25 July. $0 USD Late filing surcharge plus late-payment interest; penalty of 50% of the tax amount for untimely submission; criminal audit exposure for persistently non-compliant entities.
Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real - DTR) Within 1 month after the approval of the annual accounts; for 31 December year-end, expected by 30 July; any changes in beneficial ownership or shareholding percentages must be declared within 10 days of the relevant corporate registry event. $0 USD Failure to file or inaccuracies subject to administrative penalties up to EUR 3,000; registry closure until declaration is corrected; non-compliance can restrict public subsidies and public procurement access.
Annual VAT Summary Return (Modelo 390) For all VAT-registered Spanish SLs, due between 1 and 30 January following the close of the calendar year; zero-reporting and extensive transaction data must be included. $0 USD Late filing penalties of 50% of amounts due plus late-payment interest; loss of VAT operating regime for habitual late filing; the entity may be excluded from Censos de Empresarios, impairing invoice issuance.
Annual Related-Party Transactions Information Return (Modelo 232) Applicable when, in aggregate, related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 or when qualifying transfer pricing documentation is required; filing window is the same as the Modelo 200 — 1-25 July for 31 December year-end. $0 USD Penalty of 1,000 EUR per data item or group of omitted data (minimum 5,000 EUR); assessment against undervalued or overvalued controlled transactions and adjustment of the corporate tax base.
Annual return deadline

Approval by shareholders' meeting within first 6 months after fiscal year-end; deposit with the Commercial Registry within 1 month after approval; for 31 December year-end, latest deposit is approximately 30 July.

$0 USD

Late filing penalties

Late deposit triggers 'cierre registral' (registry closure), preventing registration of any subsequent corporate or share transfers; administrative fines up to EUR 300 and possible loss of good standing; persistent non-compliance may lead to judicial dissolution and final deregistration.

Strike-off trigger

Mandatory Audit Threshold Mandatory Audit for All Entities

Turnover: Compulsory independent audit for an SL when, at the close of two consecutive fiscal years, at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded: balance sheet total greater than EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover greater than EUR 5,700,000; average number of employees greater than 50. Audit is also compulsory for entities forming a consolidated group and for public-interest or financing-regulated entities, regardless of these thresholds.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19%

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days after the end of the six-month anniversary of the fiscal year-end. Example: calendar-year entity must file by 25 July.

Deadline: · Frequency:

First instalment due 20 April; second instalment due 20 October; third instalment due 20 December. Non-calendar tax periods shift the deadlines by the same 25-day/6-month rule.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 Taxpayer legal identification (NIF, corporate name, address). Non-resident shareholder does not enter Form 200; the Spanish SL files using its own Spanish NIF. Late filing without a prior AEAT requirement triggers surcharges: 5% (delay up to 3 months), 10% (3–6 months), 15% (6–12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest (Art. 27 LGT). If no tax is due, a €200 fixed fine applies. Filing after an AEAT request entails penalties between 50% and 100% of the amount not paid.
Box 3 Tax period start and end dates. Must match the SL's registered fiscal year. Non-calendar-year is accepted if registered with AEAT. Late filing without a prior AEAT requirement triggers surcharges: 5% (delay up to 3 months), 10% (3–6 months), 15% (6–12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest (Art. 27 LGT). If no tax is due, a €200 fixed fine applies. Filing after an AEAT request entails penalties between 50% and 100% of the amount not paid.
Boxes 208-209 Permanent and temporary differences reconciling accounting result to taxable base. For PCBA contract manufacturing, include inventory transfer pricing adjustments and intercompany expense add-backs. Non-resident parent does not file this section. Late filing without a prior AEAT requirement triggers surcharges: 5% (delay up to 3 months), 10% (3–6 months), 15% (6–12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest (Art. 27 LGT). If no tax is due, a €200 fixed fine applies. Filing after an AEAT request entails penalties between 50% and 100% of the amount not paid.
Box 260 Assessable taxable base after statutory loss carryforwards. Ensure loss-offset caps are respected; non-resident parent controls the tax group through accounting consolidation. Late filing without a prior AEAT requirement triggers surcharges: 5% (delay up to 3 months), 10% (3–6 months), 15% (6–12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest (Art. 27 LGT). If no tax is due, a €200 fixed fine applies. Filing after an AEAT request entails penalties between 50% and 100% of the amount not paid.
Box 300 Full tax quota applying the applicable rate (25% or 15%). If the SL qualifies as a new company, 15% applies; non-resident ownership does not affect the rate. Late filing without a prior AEAT requirement triggers surcharges: 5% (delay up to 3 months), 10% (3–6 months), 15% (6–12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest (Art. 27 LGT). If no tax is due, a €200 fixed fine applies. Filing after an AEAT request entails penalties between 50% and 100% of the amount not paid.
Box 399 Result of return: amount to pay or refund. Any payment due must be settled by the statutory deadline; refund is credited to the SL's Spanish bank account. Late filing without a prior AEAT requirement triggers surcharges: 5% (delay up to 3 months), 10% (3–6 months), 15% (6–12 months), 20% (over 12 months) plus late interest (Art. 27 LGT). If no tax is due, a €200 fixed fine applies. Filing after an AEAT request entails penalties between 50% and 100% of the amount not paid.
Box 1 Tax base to be used for the instalment calculation, based on the latest agreed tax assessment or accounting result. Insert the SL's own pre-offset tax base as per Spanish rules; the foreign parent's facts do not alter the instalment base. Failure to file an instalment or filing late incurs a late-filing surcharge and late interest. An inspector can assess 50%–100% penalty on the omitted instalment if there is no reasonable cause.
Box 2 Instalment calculation method (official percentage method or 60% profit-based method). For PCBA contract manufacturers, consistency with TP margins is essential. Both methods must respect arm's-length evidence. Failure to file an instalment or filing late incurs a late-filing surcharge and late interest. An inspector can assess 50%–100% penalty on the omitted instalment if there is no reasonable cause.
Box 3 Amount payable; bank direct debit reference. Instalments are not final returns but are creditable against the annual Form 200 liability. Failure to file an instalment or filing late incurs a late-filing surcharge and late interest. An inspector can assess 50%–100% penalty on the omitted instalment if there is no reasonable cause.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: EUR 250,000 aggregate annual related-party transactions (if total controlled transactions do not exceed this amount, no TP documentation obligation); Country-by-Country Report required for groups with consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to offshore financial centres, but general anti-abuse rules, CFC rules and the OECD Principal Purpose Test impose substance requirements. A PCBA contract manufacturer must have operating premises, manufacturing equipment, qualified employees, strategic risk management, and commercial decision-taking in Spain. Absent economic substance, treaty benefits may be denied, profits re-attributed to the parent, and the corporate veil may be pierced.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalty from 50% to 100% of the evaded amount plus late interest (Art. 191 LGT). Criminal prosecution under Art. 305 Penal Code imposes imprisonment of 1–6 years and a fine of 2–6 times the defrauded amount where the tax loss exceeds EUR 120,000.

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly sign false returns are criminally liable; courts may impose travel bans, attachment of personal assets, and disqualification from managing companies.
Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance

Statutory sanction: AEAT may apply anti-abuse rules (Art. 15 LGT) to recharacterise the structure; treaty benefits denied under OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test; CFC rules can attribute undistributed profits to resident shareholders; fictitious invoice penalties can reach 50% of the amount of the transactions involved.

Director personal liability: The corporate veil may be pierced, leaving directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax; complicity in sham arrangements can support criminal charges.
Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance

Statutory sanction: AEAT adjusts taxable income to the arm's-length result, adds late interest, and imposes documentation penalties: EUR 1,500 per inaccurate or incomplete data item (max EUR 15,000); complete failure to provide documentation can attract penalties up to EUR 50,000.

Director personal liability: Directors and tax advisors who knowingly certify mispriced documentation are jointly liable for the adjusted tax and interest; fraudulent TP documentation may trigger criminal liability for tax evasion.
AML / Counter-Terrorist Financing

Statutory sanction: Under Ley 10/2010, serious AML infractions are fined EUR 150,000–EUR 1,500,000; very serious cases can reach EUR 15,000,000. Criminal money-laundering under the Penal Code carries imprisonment from 1 to 10 years plus fines.

Director personal liability: Directors as obliged-entities face personal fines, suspension from commercial activity, travel restrictions, and criminal imprisonment if they knowingly facilitate laundering.
